geometry_edits.rationale: Add a carved public court while keeping the slab ancestry, so the ground edge can respond to the frontage more legibly.
Use a bounded court depth that creates usable void without over-fragmenting the mass.
Open the court toward the program-frame access side to strengthen the public threshold and street relationship.
Make the courtyard-wrapped mass the new root so the public void becomes a primary spatial organizer.

graph_edits.rationale: Preserve the dominant stepped gesture but make the public threshold explicit with a massing subtraction rather than only shallow setbacks.
Slightly deepen the stepping to improve terrace legibility and reduce the generic block-like reading.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped plate with a single readable dominant gesture across all four views. It responds well to the parcel shape without merely filling the box, and the stepped silhouette is consistent rather than arbitrary. The main weakness is public-ground articulation: the mass sits fairly sealed to the parcel with only a modest edge response to the verified frontage/access side, so the void/publicness score is only moderate. Programmatically it can plausibly support neighborhood living / small commercial mixed-use because the form reads as a compact capacity-aware street building, but it would benefit from a more explicit ground threshold or carved court to better match the active-edge brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a taller mixed-use tower; candidate is lower and more compact, so only the stepping logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked platform massing can stay legible when the stepping reads as one dominant body with controlled setbacks.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a café/restaurant object with a sign-like tower; candidate has no comparable vertical marker or canopy articulation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low horizontal base with a more vertical secondary element can create a clear public edge and compact street presence.

warnings: The access/frontage response is present but weak; consider a clearer entry seam, notch, or court aligned to the verified road edge.
The form is coherent as a single mass, but the current stepped treatment is close to a generic ziggurat unless tied more directly to public ground or terrace use.
